tool_schemas.name: get_current_weather
tool_schemas.description: Returns the latest cached current-conditions weather product for the provided US coordinate (lat,lng), including the resolved internal location and the nearest applicable observation station when available. This endpoint validates the coordinate format and range and requires the point to fall within supported US land/territories/coastal-waters coverage. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for malformed/unknown location input, NOT_FOUND when the location cannot be resolved to a supported coverage area, UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN when the caller is not permitted to access the service, and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when request-rate or quota limits are exceeded.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees. Example: '40.7128,-74.0060' for New York City. Must be within US boundaries including states, territories (PR, VI, AS, GU, MP), and coastal waters.

tool_schemas.name: get_weather_forecast
tool_schemas.description: Returns a multi-day day/night forecast product for the resolved US location for the requested number of days (1–7), using the most recent cached forecast for that point. This endpoint is not paged; it returns up to the requested number of days in a single response. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR when location parsing fails or days is outside 1–7, NOT_FOUND when the coordinate is outside supported coverage or cannot be resolved to a forecast grid, UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN for access-control failures, and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when rate/quota limits are exceeded.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees. Example: '40.7128,-74.0060' for New York City. Must be within US boundaries including states, territories (PR, VI, AS, GU, MP), and coastal waters.

days.description: Number of days to forecast (1-7, default 7). Each day includes both day and night periods.

tool_schemas.name: get_hourly_forecast
tool_schemas.description: Returns an hour-by-hour forecast time series for the resolved US location for the requested horizon (1–48 hours), using the latest cached hourly forecast available for that point. This endpoint is not paged; it returns up to the requested number of hourly periods in a single response. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR when location parsing fails or hours is outside 1–48, NOT_FOUND when the coordinate is outside supported coverage or cannot be resolved to an hourly forecast source, UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN for access-control failures, and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when rate/quota limits are exceeded.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees. Example: '40.7128,-74.0060' for New York City. Must be within US boundaries including states, territories (PR, VI, AS, GU, MP), and coastal waters.

hours.description: Number of hours to forecast (1-48, default 24). Provides temperature, conditions, and precipitation probability for each hour.

tool_schemas.name: get_weather_alerts
tool_schemas.description: Returns active NWS-style alerts (watches/warnings/advisories) for a specific point (lat,lng) or for a 2-letter state/territory code, optionally filtered by severity; results are returned as a single list (not paged). This endpoint validates that location is either a coordinate pair or a recognized code and that severity is one of: all, extreme, severe, moderate, minor. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for invalid location/severity, NOT_FOUND when the location code is unrecognized or the point cannot be mapped to a supported alert region, UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN for access-control failures, and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when rate/quota limits are exceeded.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees OR 2-letter state/territory code. Examples: '40.7128,-74.0060' for New York City, 'CA' for California, 'PR' for Puerto Rico. Valid state codes: AL, AK, AS, AR, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DE, DC, FL, GA, GU, HI, ID, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, LA, ME, MD, MA, MI, MN, MS, MO, MT, NE, NV, NH, NJ, NM, NY, NC, ND, OH, OK, OR, PA, PR, RI, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VT, VI, VA, WA, WV, WI, WY, MP, PW, FM, MH.

severity.description: Filter by alert severity: 'extreme' (life-threatening), 'severe' (significant threat), 'moderate' (possible threat), 'minor' (minimal threat), or 'all' (default - shows all active alerts).

tool_schemas.name: find_weather_stations
tool_schemas.description: Returns up to limit nearby weather observation stations for the resolved US coordinate, ordered by increasing distance from the point; the response includes the resolved internal location and station metadata. This endpoint is not paged; it returns up to 20 stations in a single response according to the limit parameter. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for malformed coordinates or limit outside 1–20, NOT_FOUND when the coordinate is outside supported coverage or no station index is available for the resolved location, UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN for access-control failures, and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when rate/quota limits are exceeded.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees. Example: '40.7128,-74.0060' for New York City. Must be within US boundaries including states, territories (PR, VI, AS, GU, MP), and coastal waters.

limit.description: Maximum number of stations to return (1-20, default 10). Stations are returned ordered by distance from the specified location.

tool_schemas.implementation:
def find_weather_stations(location, limit=None, **_extra):
    import json, os, datetime, re, math, time
    _DB = __import__("os").environ.get("MCP_DB_DIR") or ("./environment_mix/0026000" if __import__("os").path.isdir("./environment_mix/0026000") else "/app/database")
    def _load(n):
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f)
        except Exception: return []
    def _save(n, d):
        with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(d, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    def _err(code, msg, **x): return {"error": {"code": code, "message": msg, **x}}

    t0 = time.time()
    now = datetime.datetime.utcnow().replace(microsecond=0).isoformat() + "Z"

    def _new_id(prefix):
        return f"{prefix}_{datetime.datetime.utcnow().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}_{os.urandom(6).hex()}"

    def _log(status, http_code, location_id=None, error_message=None, cache_hit=False, served_weather_product_id=None, limit_v=None):
        reqs = _load("api_requests.json")
        rid = _new_id("req")
        row = {
            "id": rid,
            "tool_name": "find_weather_stations",
            "location_raw": location if isinstance(location, str) else str(location),
            "location_id": location_id,
            "days": None,
            "hours": None,
            "limit": limit_v,
            "severity": None,
            "response_status_code": http_code,
            "cache_hit": bool(cache_hit),
            "served_weather_product_id": served_weather_product_id,
            "latency_ms": int(max(0, round((time.time() - t0) * 1000))),
            "status": status,
            "error_message": error_message,
            "created_at": now,
            "updated_at": now,
        }
        reqs.append(row)
        _save("api_requests.json", reqs)

    def _parse_coords(s):
        if not isinstance(s, str):
            return None
        m = re.match(r"^\s*-?\d+(\.\d+)?\s*,\s*-?\d+(\.\d+)?\s*$", s)
        if not m:
            return None
        parts = s.split(",")
        try:
            lat = float(parts[0].strip())
            lon = float(parts[1].strip())
        except ValueError:
            return None
        return lat, lon

    # US boundaries (approx) including territories/coastal waters
    def _within_us(lat, lon):
        if lat is None or lon is None:
            return False
        # CONUS + AK/HI broad bounds
        if (24.0 <= lat <= 49.8 and -125.0 <= lon <= -66.0):
            return True
        if (51.0 <= lat <= 71.5 and -170.0 <= lon <= -129.0):  # Alaska
            return True
        if (18.5 <= lat <= 22.6 and -160.5 <= lon <= -154.5):  # Hawaii
            return True
        # PR / VI
        if (17.5 <= lat <= 18.7 and -67.5 <= lon <= -64.2):
            return True
        # Guam / MP
        if (13.0 <= lat <= 20.6 and 144.5 <= lon <= 146.5):
            return True
        # American Samoa (crosses -170..-168)
        if (-15.0 <= lat <= -10.0 and -171.5 <= lon <= -167.0):
            return True
        # Micronesia / Marshall Islands / Palau (US-associated, allowed set includes FM/MH/PW)
        if (1.0 <= lat <= 10.5 and 131.0 <= lon <= 163.5):
            return True
        return False

    def _haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
        R = 6371.0
        p1 = math.radians(lat1); p2 = math.radians(lat2)
        dphi = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)
        dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)
        a = math.sin(dphi/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dl/2)**2
        return 2 * R * math.asin(min(1.0, math.sqrt(a)))

    # Validate limit
    if limit is None:
        limit_v = 10
    else:
        if not isinstance(limit, (int, float)) or isinstance(limit, bool):
            _log("rejected", 400, error_message="limit must be a number between 1 and 20", limit_v=None)
            return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "limit must be a number between 1 and 20")
        limit_v = int(limit)
    if limit_v < 1 or limit_v > 20:
        _log("rejected", 400, error_message="limit must be between 1 and 20", limit_v=limit_v)
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "limit must be between 1 and 20")

    coords = _parse_coords(location)
    if not coords:
        _log("rejected", 400, error_message="Malformed coordinates. Expected 'lat,lng'.", limit_v=limit_v)
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "Malformed coordinates. Expected 'lat,lng'.")
    lat, lon = coords
    if not (-90.0 <= lat <= 90.0 and -180.0 <= lon <= 180.0):
        _log("rejected", 400, error_message="Coordinates out of range.", limit_v=limit_v)
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "Coordinates out of range.")
    if not _within_us(lat, lon):
        _log("rejected", 400, error_message="Coordinates not within supported US boundaries.", limit_v=limit_v)
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "Coordinates not within supported US boundaries.")

    # Resolve/create location row (derived_from_coordinates)
    locations = _load("locations.json")
    # Uniqueness: unique(source, input_location_raw). For tools, use derived_from_coordinates.
    source_key = "derived_from_coordinates"
    input_raw_norm = f"{lat:.6f},{lon:.6f}"
    existing = None
    for r in locations:
        if r.get("source") == source_key and r.get("input_location_raw") == input_raw_norm:
            existing = r
            break
    if existing:
        if existing.get("status") == "blocked":
            _log("failed", 404, location_id=existing.get("id"), error_message="Location is blocked.", limit_v=limit_v)
            return _err("NOT_FOUND", "Location cannot be used.")
        location_row = existing
        location_row["updated_at"] = now
        _save("locations.json", locations)
    else:
        loc_id = _new_id("loc")
        location_row = {
            "id": loc_id,
            "source": source_key,
            "input_location_raw": input_raw_norm,
            "latitude": lat,
            "longitude": lon,
            "state_code": None,
            "timezone": None,
            "coverage_type": "unknown",
            "status": "active",
            "created_at": now,
            "updated_at": now,
        }
        locations.append(location_row)
        _save("locations.json", locations)

    stations = _load("stations.json")
    active = []
    for st in stations:
        if st.get("status") != "active":
            continue
        st_lat = st.get("latitude"); st_lon = st.get("longitude")
        if not isinstance(st_lat, (int, float)) or not isinstance(st_lon, (int, float)):
            continue
        dkm = _haversine_km(lat, lon, float(st_lat), float(st_lon))
        active.append((dkm, st))

    active.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    selected = active[:limit_v]
    out = []
    for dkm, st in selected:
        out.append({
            "id": st.get("id"),
            "station_code": st.get("station_code"),
            "name": st.get("name"),
            "station_type": st.get("station_type"),
            "latitude": st.get("latitude"),
            "longitude": st.get("longitude"),
            "elevation_m": st.get("elevation_m"),
            "state_code": st.get("state_code"),
            "distance_km": round(dkm, 3),
            "status": st.get("status"),
            "updated_at": st.get("updated_at"),
        })

    _log("succeeded", 200, location_id=location_row.get("id"), cache_hit=False, limit_v=limit_v)
    return {
        "location": {
            "id": location_row.get("id"),
            "source": location_row.get("source"),
            "input_location_raw": location_row.get("input_location_raw"),
            "latitude": location_row.get("latitude"),
            "longitude": location_row.get("longitude"),
            "state_code": location_row.get("state_code"),
            "timezone": location_row.get("timezone"),
            "coverage_type": location_row.get("coverage_type"),
            "status": location_row.get("status"),
            "created_at": location_row.get("created_at"),
            "updated_at": location_row.get("updated_at"),
        },
        "stations": out,
        "limit": limit_v,
        "total_returned": len(out),
    }

tool_schemas.name: get_local_time
tool_schemas.description: Returns the current local time at the resolved US coordinate, including the timezone used to compute the local timestamp. This endpoint validates coordinate format/range and resolves the point to a supported US timezone. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for malformed coordinates, NOT_FOUND when the coordinate cannot be resolved to a supported US location/timezone, UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN for access-control failures, and TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when rate/quota limits are exceeded.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees. Example: '40.7128,-74.0060' for New York City.

tool_schemas.name: resolve_location
tool_schemas.description: Resolves a user-provided US location into a normalized internal locations record. Accepts either coordinates (lat,lng) or a 2-letter state/territory code; validates inputs, enforces US coverage rules for coordinate resolution, and returns the existing matching location when present or creates/updates a normalized record when allowed. Refuses malformed coordinates/state codes and rejects coordinates outside supported US land/territories/coastal-waters coverage.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees OR 2-letter state/territory code. Examples: '40.7128,-74.0060' or 'CA'. Coordinates must match '^\\s*-?\\d+(\\.\\d+)?\\s*,\\s*-?\\d+(\\.\\d+)?\\s*$' and be within supported US boundaries.

source.description: Optional source tag stored on the resolved location record.

create_if_missing.description: When true (default), creates a new locations record if no suitable normalized location exists; when false, returns NOT_FOUND if the location cannot be resolved to an existing record.

tool_schemas.name: refresh_weather_products
tool_schemas.description: Triggers an asynchronous refresh of cached NWS-style products for a resolved location. The service enqueues provider fetch/ingest work and returns the most recent cached products immediately when available; it refuses invalid coordinates/state codes and will not serve status='error' unless no other product exists. Use this to proactively refresh current conditions, forecasts, and/or alerts.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees OR 2-letter state/territory code. Coordinates must be within supported US boundaries; state codes must be recognized for alerts refresh.

kinds.description: Which product kinds to refresh. 'forecast_daily' corresponds to daily (days=N) variants; 'forecast_hourly' corresponds to hourly (hours=N) variants.

days.description: Daily forecast horizon used when kinds includes 'forecast_daily' (1–7).

hours.description: Hourly forecast horizon used when kinds includes 'forecast_hourly' (1–48).

severity.description: Alert severity variant used when kinds includes 'alerts'.

force.description: When true, refreshes even if a fresh cached product exists; when false, refreshes only when fresh data is missing or expiring.

tool_schemas.name: list_api_requests
tool_schemas.description: Lists recent API request audit records with optional filters. Returns a paginated list ordered by created_at descending. Refuses invalid filter combinations and enforces safe pagination limits.

tool_name.description: Filter by the tool name that generated the audit record (e.g., 'get_current_weather').

location_id.description: Filter by resolved internal location id.

response_status_code.description: Filter by HTTP-like response status code recorded for the request.

cache_hit.description: Filter by whether the request was served from cache.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return per page (1–100).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned from a previous call.

start_at.description: Only include requests created at or after this timestamp (RFC 3339).

end_at.description: Only include requests created before this timestamp (RFC 3339).

tool_schemas.name: get_api_request
tool_schemas.description: Fetches a single API request audit record by id. Returns the full stored request metadata including validated parameters, cache flags, and any error details. Refuses unknown ids with NOT_FOUND.

id.description: Primary key of the api_requests record to fetch.

tool_schemas.name: update_location_status
tool_schemas.description: Transitions a locations record between lifecycle states by updating its status. Only allows declared transitions: active→inactive/blocked, inactive→active/blocked, blocked→inactive. Refuses invalid transitions and unknown ids.

id.description: Primary key of the locations record to update.

status.description: New lifecycle status for the location; must be a valid transition from the current status.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason for the status change (stored for audit/debugging).

tool_schemas.name: get_whoami
tool_schemas.description: Returns the calling identity and authorization context for the current credential, including granted scopes and current rate-limit/quota consumption where applicable. Refuses missing/invalid credentials with UNAUTHORIZED.

api_key.description: API key credential used to authenticate this request.
